newsitem.title: UK: UK forecasters see drier, warmer weather next week.
newsitem.headline: UK forecasters see drier, warmer weather next week.

text.p: UK forecasters predict summer weather for much of next week, after the wettest June this century, according to the Meteorological Office.

"Drier, warmer and sunnier weather will gradually set in over the weekend, heralding a welcome change for many people that will continue well into next week," the Meteorological Office said in a statement.
However, the north-west will be cloudier and thundery showers may break out later in the week, although it will stay warm.

After a record dry start to the year, heavy rain has triggered concern about the quality of developing British grains crops, as well as the possible effect of rain on the harvest, due to start in a few weeks.
Despite the rain, Britain's drought has not ended, according to the Environment Agency.

Although June's rainfall has been useful in cutting the need for irrigation and watering of gardens, the rainfall is not reaching aquifers, where levels remain low, the agency said, in a statement on Wednesday.
